title: Adopt STUDY_AI single-project feature layout, retire four skills, and restore real flows
description: Starting from PR #34 head bf8c365, adopt the STUDY_AI-style single deployable API with feature folders (never separate Api/Business/Data projects), safely retire the standalone Listening/Speaking/Reading/Writing modules, repair EF migrations/routes/contracts, split unit and integration tests, remove production mock fallbacks, and verify every remaining Admin, Content Manager, Teacher, Support and Student flow against real APIs and isolated SQL Server.
phase: Reference-layout migration and full functional acceptance
architecture_decisions: Use one deployable backend project at Backend/src/ZhongWenHub.Api, matching the reference repository's StudyAI.Api shape
Do not create separate Api, Business or Data class-library projects
Keep Data as an internal folder for ApplicationDbContext and initialization only
Co-locate controller, DTO, validation, service and feature-specific persistence behavior under Features/<Feature>
Use the reference repository for folder/navigation principles only; do not copy its domain code
retired_features: Standalone Speaking skill module and /skills/speaking plus legacy /speaking
known_blockers: EF migrations target ApplicationDbContext while runtime migration uses AppDbContext
AddMultiProviderAiConfigurations designer and model snapshot are incomplete
Two teacher submission routes contain duplicated route prefixes
Swagger integration test rewrites its own route baseline
Active AI bridge scripts reference removed backend paths
CI does not provision SQL Server or enforce integration tests
Frontend production flows require a zero-mock real-API audit
Retired skill routes, navigation, mock fixtures, deep links and exclusive speaking services remain active
acceptance_criteria: Exactly one production API project, one unit-test project and one integration-test project exist under Backend
No separate Api, Business or Data production project exists; Data is only an internal folder of ZhongWenHub.Api
ApplicationDbContext is the only real EF context used by runtime, Identity, migrations and tests
Fresh and upgrade migration paths pass on disposable SQL Server without manual DDL
AiProviderConfigurations exists once and EF model snapshot matches the runtime model
Teacher submission detail and grade routes are absolute and contain no duplicated prefix
OpenAPI route comparison is read-only and fails on method/path regression
Unit and integration tests are split without losing unique coverage or double-counting
Identity, JWT, role authorization and ownership checks remain functional with a simple local configuration
Production has no MockAIProvider, fake LLM success, static admin success data or silent API fallback
Admin Multi-Provider AI CRUD, testing, priorities, masking, usage and failover work with real persistence
Admin, Content Manager, Teacher, Support and Student frontend flows use real APIs and persist after reload
Listening, Speaking, Reading and Writing standalone routes, navigation, pages, mocks and exclusive runtime APIs are removed
Legacy skill URLs redirect to /practice while shared lesson reading/listening content, audio/video playback and general AI Tutor remain functional
Historical migrations and existing skill data are preserved; retirement introduces no table drop or destructive data migration
Backend CI provisions isolated SQL Server and executes integration tests
Backend unit/integration tests, frontend lint/tests/build and role Playwright flows pass
ZhongWenHub_Dev remains unchanged under zero-write policy
safety_constraints: Never write to ZhongWenHub_Dev or production databases
Never execute manual DDL as a substitute for EF migration repair
Never edit applied migration Up or Down operations; use forward-only correction when needed
Never commit real JWT secrets, provider keys, email credentials or database passwords
Never expose provider keys in API responses or logs
Do not copy domain code or fake providers from the reference repository
Do not create separate Api, Business or Data class-library projects
Do not delete historical migrations, drop retired-skill tables or erase existing user data
Do not remove shared lesson text/audio/video capabilities based only on skill-related names
Do not introduce microservices, MediatR, CQRS, generic repositories, custom UnitOfWork or enterprise permission infrastructure
Do not force-push or merge directly to main
Do not claim blocked, skipped or unexecuted tests as passed
